Theme

Household, washing & chores

mirror noun

also look in the mirror, look at oneself in the mirror, look into the mirror

classical

Plaut.
Varro, LL 5.129
Traupman 167

speculum, speculī n.

noun, second declension

Examples

  • in speculō spectāre

    look in the mirrorcomposed

  • pater autem, post eum stāns et in speculō spectāns, id perfēcit quod puer coeperat

    Dad, standing behind him and watching in the mirror, finished what the boy had begunLibellus I, Iter in Lūsitāniam

  • sē in speculō intuērī

    to look at oneself in the mirrorTraupman 346

  • in speculum īnspicere

    to look into the mirrorTraupman 346

See also washbasin, reflect.

SourcesLewis & Short: speculum

Theodōrus et pater · Ad Larem avītum, Libellī I–VII, as they stood on 7 November 2026. Examples marked “Libellus” quote those texts word for word.

The example sentence marked “composed” is ours.

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 167, each phrase checked against the searchable text of the book.
